source_note: Curated from AARP, Cleveland Clinic, Kaiser Permanente, and NIA-style geriatric guidance. Low-intensity, knee-aware. MUST be reviewed with your care team before use; this is a starting template, not medical advice.

exercises.name: Ankle Circles
steps: Sit tall in a sturdy chair with your feet flat on the floor.
Lift your right foot a few inches off the floor.
Draw 10 slow circles with your toes, then reverse for 10 more.
Lower the foot and repeat with the left.
exercises.seatedVariant: This exercise is done seated — no change needed.
exercises.safetyCue: Move slowly and keep the motion at the ankle. Stop if you feel any pinch in the knee.

exercises.name: Seated Marching
steps: Sit tall, hands resting on your thighs or lightly on the sides of the chair.
Lift one knee a comfortable height, then set the foot down.
Alternate legs in a slow, steady march.
Aim for about 20 lifts total, breathing easily throughout.
exercises.seatedVariant: This exercise is done seated. If you'd like more, you can march in place while holding the back of the chair.
exercises.safetyCue: Only lift as high as feels easy. Keep your back supported.

exercises.name: Shoulder Rolls
steps: Sit or stand tall with arms relaxed at your sides.
Slowly roll both shoulders up toward your ears, then back and down.
Repeat 8 times backward, then 8 times forward.
exercises.seatedVariant: This exercise is done seated — no change needed.
exercises.safetyCue: Keep the movement gentle and smooth; no need to force the range.

exercises.name: Gentle Neck Turns
steps: Sit tall with your shoulders relaxed and eyes forward.
Slowly turn your head to look over your right shoulder.
Hold for a breath, return to center, then turn to the left.
Repeat 5 times to each side.
exercises.seatedVariant: This exercise is done seated — no change needed.
exercises.safetyCue: Turn only as far as is comfortable. Never force or jerk the neck.

exercises.name: Seated Knee Extensions
steps: Sit tall with both feet flat and about hip-width apart.
Slowly straighten one leg out in front, as far as is comfortable.
Hold for a moment, then lower with control.
Do about 10 on each leg, alternating.
exercises.seatedVariant: This exercise is done seated — gentle and good for the knee.
exercises.safetyCue: Don't lock the knee or push into pain. A gentle stretch behind the knee is fine.

exercises.name: Heel-to-Toe Weight Shifts
steps: Stand behind a sturdy chair, both hands resting on the back.
Slowly rock your weight onto your heels, lifting your toes.
Then rock forward onto the balls of your feet, lifting your heels.
Repeat 10 slow shifts, keeping a light hold on the chair.
exercises.seatedVariant: Seated: with feet flat, lift your toes, then your heels, alternating, about 10 times.
exercises.safetyCue: Keep a hand on the chair the whole time. Stop if you feel unsteady.

exercises.name: Supported Single-Leg Stand
steps: Stand behind a sturdy chair, holding the back with both hands.
Shift your weight onto one foot and lift the other slightly off the floor.
Hold for 5 to 10 seconds, then lower.
Repeat 3 to 5 times on each side.
exercises.seatedVariant: Seated: straighten one leg and hold it lifted a few inches for 5 seconds, then switch.
exercises.safetyCue: Keep both hands on the chair. Only lift the foot a little. Stop if wobbly.

exercises.name: Sit-to-Stand Chair Rises
steps: Sit toward the front of a sturdy chair, feet flat and hip-width apart.
Lean slightly forward and press through your heels to stand.
Use the armrests for help if you need them.
Lower back down slowly with control. Repeat about 5 times.
exercises.seatedVariant: Seated: lean forward as if to rise and gently press into your legs without fully standing, 5 times.
exercises.safetyCue: Use the armrests freely. Keep the range small and pain-free for your knee.

exercises.name: Seated Torso Twist
steps: Sit tall with feet flat and hands resting on your thighs.
Gently turn your upper body to the right, letting your gaze follow.
Hold for a breath, return to center, then turn left.
Repeat 5 times each way.
exercises.seatedVariant: This exercise is done seated — no change needed.
exercises.safetyCue: Twist from the waist gently; keep your hips facing forward. No forcing.

exercises.name: Seated Hamstring & Calf Stretch
steps: Sit tall toward the front of the chair.
Extend one leg out with the heel on the floor and toes pointing up.
Sit a little taller and lean forward gently until you feel a mild stretch.
Hold for 15 to 20 seconds, then switch legs.
exercises.seatedVariant: This exercise is done seated — no change needed.
exercises.safetyCue: A mild stretch is the goal, never pain. Keep your back long rather than rounding.
